decisive_items: ST segments elevated 4-6 mm in leads II, III and aVF, with ST depression in leads V2-V6
Widespread ST-segment elevations (4-15 mm) in leads II, III, aVF, and V2-V6
10% stenosis in proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) and right coronary artery (RCA)
response.rationale: Transient ST elevations with nonobstructive coronaries and alcohol-triggered syncope/arrhythmias indicate coronary vasospasm (variant angina), not fixed CAD, cardiomyopathy, or primary arrhythmia.

rejected.why: No evidence of hypertrophy or obstruction; ECG and angiographic findings point to vasospasm, not HCM.
Alcohol history alone does not explain transient ST elevations and syncope; no heart failure or cardiomyopathy features are present.
